inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted 465,625,663 (FY2026 AR Note 8 EPS reconciliation, line 13887; ordinary shares on issue at year-end 467M). Held FLAT because SBC (0.33% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows -- charging both would double-count. No formal buyback program; the Feb-2026 Havilah/Kalkaroo consideration included some Sandfire scrip but that is non-operating M&A currency, not compensation, and is captured via the equity bridge instead of share-count growth.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report Note 27 'Share-based payments': total expense 5,494 (line 15126: SFR 5,313 + SFRA/Sandfire Resources America 181). No separate equity-award net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed and no combined 'adjusted' SBC figure is published, so the Note-27 cash-flow-statement figure is used directly. Immaterial at 0.33% of revenue -- this is not an SBC-driven valuation.
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback program; ShareRepurchases is not disclosed/populated. FY26 capital return was via dividend (35 AUD cents/share final, first since 2022), not repurchases.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and every driver are in US dollars (Sandfire switched presentation currency AUD->USD effective FY2022 to align with USD-denominated copper sales; pre-FY2022 rows in the CSV are legacy AUD DeGrussa-era and are NOT used in this build). The ASX quote is AUD. All per-share values are computed in USD then converted at USD/AUD 1.4249 = 1/0.7018 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X regularMarketPrice 0.7018 at 2026-09-25T ~within the hour of the price fetch). No liquid USD-quoted dual listing exists for a parity check (Sandfire delisted from LSE/JSE/TSX years ago); cross-check instead against the FY26 Annual Report's own AUD dividend declaration (35 AUD cents = US$0.246 at this rate, consistent with a USD-denominated but AUD-administered payment) and against FY27 guidance which is entirely USD-denominated, confirming USD is the correct flows currency. The unsuffixed intrinsic values and weighted_iv are in AUD (the quote currency) so they compare directly to current_price; USD twins are the model-currency basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-built, because the flows are USD (copper is a globally USD-denominated commodity, the statements are US$m, FY27 guidance is entirely USD): US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium (a touch above the FMG.AX/IGO.AX 5.0% house default given SFR's smaller scale, ~sub-1% global market share and two-producing-asset concentration), equity beta ~1.3 for a small pure-play polymetallic copper miner, giving a cost of equity of ~11.3%. Company is net-cash with zero bank debt at FY26 year-end, so pre-tax cost of debt is a nominal placeholder (~6.5%, ~4.9% after 25% Australian/Spanish/Botswana blended tax) at a notional 5% target gearing for WACC-weighting purposes only (actual gearing is negative). Weights ~95% equity / 5% notional debt give ~10.9%, rounded to 11.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; single-commodity exposure, two-asset concentration, TC/RC cyclicality and jurisdictional risk (Spain/Botswana/Australia) are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Lease liabilities of 36.432 (23.274 current + 13.158 non-current, FY2026 AR Note 14, lines 12848/12853) are INCLUDED in total_debt (bank borrowings 0 + leases 36.432 = 36.432) and hence in net_debt: 36.432 - cash 352.629 = -316.197 (net cash). Lease principal (repayment of principal portion of lease liabilities, 24.154 in FY26 financing activities, line 12971) is therefore NOT deducted from the flows; last_fcf = reported FCF 506.896 (OCF 746.804 - capex 239.908) - SBC 5.494 - interest income 0 = 501.92. Leases are immaterial here (1.5% of revenue, 10% of net PP&E) so no separate lease-renewal capex add-on is modelled; capex_pct already captures ongoing fleet/facility renewal at both sites.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial and not separately charged. NCI equity is -6.596 (FY2026, from Sandfire Resources America's ~13% public minority) and NCI's share of FY26 comprehensive income was -1.770, both rounding-level against total equity of 2,211.646 and NPAT of 355.807. FY2026 net profit used for basic/diluted EPS (355,807, Note 8) is attributable-to-parent and ties closely to reported group NPAT, confirming no material NCI leakage needs modelling.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, with the section 7 cyclical/non-US adaptations (USD flows vs AUD quote, leases as debt, risk charged once), on a MID-CYCLE basis -- required because Sandfire is a pure-play copper miner whose FY26 result (52.5% EBITDA margin, record US$1,654M revenue) sits at the confluence of two simultaneously favourable but cyclical/reversible tailwinds: a strong realised copper price (~US$11,900-12,017/t, up from ~US$9,200/t in FY25) and deeply negative treatment/refining charges (spot ~-US$126.80/t mid-2026, a smelter-capacity-glut condition that is itself cyclical). FY27 guidance is built on an even HIGHER forward copper price assumption (US$13,280/t) than FY26's realised price, and spot copper (~US$6.75/lb / ~US$14,880/t on COMEX as of valuation date) is higher still -- so neither FY26 actuals nor FY27 guidance is a repeatable base; both describe the top of the current cycle, not its middle. Only 5 fiscal years (FY2022-FY2026, all USD-reported) reflect the CURRENT asset base (MATSA acquired May-2022, Motheo first production Feb-2023); the pre-FY2022 AUD-reported history is the closed, unrelated DeGrussa single-asset business and is excluded from margin/growth judgment (used only for context on Sandfire's multi-decade operating history). Across FY2022-FY2026 EBITDA margins were 48.5% / 33.4% (MATSA-integration/Motheo-construction trough) / 38.5% / 45.9% / 52.5% (peak) -- mean 43.8%, median 45.9%, both skewed up by the two most recent (peak-cycle) years. BASE CASE sets FY27 close to FY26 (management guidance, minus a haircut for the guided forward price being above FY26 realised), then fades the EBITDA margin down to a 40% mid-cycle level by FY30 as copper price and, especially, TC/RCs mean-revert (TC/RCs swinging back toward smelters absorbing more of the value chain is the single largest identified swing factor -- Analysis JSON risks.financial), holding 40% thereafter -- below the 5-year mean/median because both are cycle-peak-skewed, and roughly midway between the FY2023 trough (33.4%, itself capex/ramp-distorted) and the FY2025-26 level. INTEREST INCOME: NOT stripped -- finance income is only 6.289 (0.4% of revenue) against net cash of 316-353M, well under the >1x-FCF-base threshold (FCF base ~502M) that triggers the strip; the cash pile is not being double-counted at this scale. LAST_FCF: 501.92 = reported FCF 506.896 (OCF 746.804 - capex 239.908) - SBC 5.494 - interest income 0. CASH TAX: FY26 cash tax paid was 91.301 against EBIT of ~549.8 (Underlying EBIT 548.528), an effective cash rate of ~16.6%, well below the 30% Australian / Spanish (25%) / Botswana (22%) combination implied by the group's multi-jurisdiction footprint -- FY26's low cash rate reflects tax losses/allowances carried from the FY2023 trough and MATSA capital allowances still being utilised; these will not persist once the loss carryforwards are exhausted. The model RAMPS the cash tax rate from FY26's low actual toward a 28% blended statutory rate (weighted toward Spain's 25% general/ MATSA's mining regime and Australia's 30% corporate rate on the smaller domestic/corporate cost base, Botswana's 22% having limited weight since Motheo is young and generating fewer local profits taxed yet) by FY29, held thereafter. ANALYSIS JSON: research/SFR.AX/Reports/SFR.AX_Analysis.json used directly for bull/bear axes, business model, risks and guidance (2026-09-25 vintage). PRICE: ASX regular-close print via Yahoo chart API, not after-hours.

sanity_multiples_memo: At A$22.445 and USD/AUD 1.4249, market cap is ~A$10.45bn (US$7.34bn, 465.626M diluted shares); EV (ex net cash of US$316.2M) ~US$7.03bn. FY2026 Underlying EBITDA 867.019 gives EV/EBITDA ~8.1x on the cyclical-peak year; on the base-case mid-cycle EBITDA (revenue held near FY26 then 40% margin, ~US$650-680M) EV/EBITDA is ~10.3-10.8x. P/B ~3.3x on equity 2,211.646; P/E ~20.6x on FY26 statutory NPAT 355.807 (peak-cycle earnings), or higher on a mid-cycle NPAT estimate. Owner-FCF yield ~6.8% on FY2026's peak 501.92 but materially lower on the mid-cycle component build. The stock has re-rated hard off the FY26 result and current TC/RC tailwind (52-week range A$13.33-25.00); analyst consensus targets (A$18.50-19.60 per Analysis JSON) sit below the current price, consistent with the view that FY26/FY27 near-term strength is substantially priced in.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal revenue growth once the FY26/27 price and TC/RC tailwinds fade, not a historical CAGR. Revenue and FCF CAGRs over FY2022-FY2026 are dominated by two structural, one-time step-changes (MATSA's May-2022 acquisition and Motheo's Feb-2023 first production ramping to full nameplate) plus the current cyclical price/TC-RC peak, none of which are organic run-rate growth; EPS/FCF CAGRs are not meaningful because FY2023 was negative on both (net loss, negative FCF from Motheo construction capex) and FY2022 predates full-year MATSA/Motheo contribution. Equity 5yr CAGR of 5.9% is the least distorted of the available series (funded mostly by retained earnings, no equity raises since the MATSA acquisition scrip in 2022) but still spans the same construction-to-peak window.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR (+20.4%) and 5yr CAGR (+12.4%) diverge sharply from equity CAGR (9.9%/5.9%) and are NOT used as growth proxies -- both windows are anchored on the FY2023 MATSA-integration trough or the FY2022 partial-year MATSA base, and both endpoints sit at different points of the copper price/TC-RC cycle (FY2023 weak copper + normal TC/RCs; FY2026 strong copper + deeply negative TC/RCs). No historical revenue or FCF CAGR is usable as a forward growth proxy for the same reason FMG.AX's iron-ore CAGRs are unusable: the endpoints are cycle-dependent, not trend-dependent.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not reported (fcf_3yr_cagr/fcf_5yr_cagr left null) because the FY2023 owner FCF was negative (-215.2, Motheo construction capex peak) and a CAGR through a negative value is not meaningful. The FY2022-FY2026 owner-FCF path (US$m): 181.5, -215.2, 116.9, 316.9, 501.9 -- is itself the mid-cycle sanity anchor: it never averages to the FY2026 figure, and even a simple 5-year mean (180.4) sits well below FY2026, consistent with the base case's mid-cycle owner FCF landing materially below the FY26 peak once the margin fades to 40%.

base.growth_note: FY2027 +1%: CuEq guided 150-166kt (midpoint 158kt, +2.5% on FY26's 154.2kt) but the FY27 forward price assumption (Cu US$13,280/t) is above FY26's realised US$11,900-12,017/t, so revenue growth is held to +1% rather than the guidance-implied higher figure -- the extra guided price uplift is treated as unearned until realised. FY2028-29 -2%/-2% as copper price and TC/RCs mean-revert down from the current cycle peak (COMEX spot ~US$6.75/lb / ~US$14,880/t as of the valuation date is itself above even FY27 guidance, underscoring how extended the current price is). FY2030 flat, then +1%/+2% nominal thereafter on modest volume growth (Motheo A1 reserve, MATSA sulphide extensions) at a normalised price.
base.margin_note: FY26 actual 52.5% (Underlying 52%). FY2027 50.0% reflects one more strong-but-moderating year on FY27's own opex guidance (Underlying Operating Unit Cost ~US$90/t MATSA, ~US$47/t Motheo, incremental vs FY26's US$89/US$46) while TC/RCs are still deeply negative. The margin then fades over FY2028-2031 to a 40% mid-cycle floor as (a) copper price normalises from the current extended level toward a longer-run average and (b) TC/RCs mean-revert from the current smelter-glut extreme back toward a level that is a genuine cost rather than a credit -- both of the Analysis JSON's identified 'financial risk' swing factors (TC/RC volatility; commodity price volatility) acting together. 40% sits above the FY2023 trough (33.4%, additionally distorted by MATSA integration and Motheo pre-production costs) and below the FY2025-26 range (45.9%/52.5%), consistent with a genuinely mid-cycle read rather than either extreme.
base.capex_note: FY2027 18.0% = guided total capex US$299M / FY27 revenue estimate (~US$1.67-1.7bn) ~ 17.6-18%, rounded up for conservatism; includes the accelerated Kalkaroo PFS spend (~US$51-70M) which is discretionary growth capital layered on top of MATSA/Motheo sustaining and development capex. Fades to a 15% steady state by FY2031 as the MATSA tailings dam and Motheo Stage 4 cutback complete and Kalkaroo, if it proceeds past PFS, would represent a separate investment decision not yet modelled (the Havilah option is carried in the equity bridge at cost, not as committed development capex).
base.da_note: FY26 D&A (318.491, Metrics CSV FY2026, from underlying reconciliation) / revenue 1,653.666 = 19.3%; FY27 guided D&A of US$369M / an estimated ~US$1.67bn FY27 revenue is ~22.1%, so the path opens at 21.0% and steps to a 22.0% steady state as the larger post-capex-program asset base (MATSA tailings dam, Motheo Stage 4, any Kalkaroo development) depreciates against a lower mid-cycle revenue base.
base.tax_note: FY26 cash tax paid (91.301, KPI CashTaxesPaid) / Underlying EBIT (548.528) = 16.6% cash rate, well below the ~28% blended statutory rate implied by Spain (25% general corporate, MATSA also subject to a mining-specific regime), Australia (30% corporate on the smaller domestic cost base) and Botswana (22%, but Motheo is young with limited local taxable profit yet). The low FY26 cash rate reflects loss carryforwards/capital allowances from the FY2023 MATSA-integration trough and Motheo's construction-phase capital allowances still being drawn down; these are a temporary tax shelter, not a repeatable feature, so the rate is RAMPED from 17% (FY27) to 28% (FY30+) rather than perpetuated at FY26's level.
base.wc_note: A concentrate producer/exporter with trade receivables (funded partly by provisional pricing) and inventories (concentrate stockpiles at MATSA/Motheo, consumables) that structurally exceed trade payables; -8% capture on the revenue change, so the FY2028-29 revenue contraction releases a little cash and later modest growth consumes a little -- consistent with the manufacturer/distributor sign convention in the adaptations file, not a prepaid/subscription model.
base.terminal_note: 12x owner-FCF cap (Gordon at 11.0%/2.0% would be 11.1x, so Gordon already binds narrowly below the cap in this case) reflects a mid-tier single-commodity miner with a depleting, though genuinely long-life (targeted 15-year reserve life at both operations), resource base and real re-rating optionality from Kalkaroo; 12x is between FMG.AX's 10x (single-commodity major, no growth optionality priced) and a growth-miner multiple, recognising SFR's Kalkaroo/MATSA-sulphide/Motheo-A1 exploration upside without assuming it converts.

bull.margin_note: Electrification/AI-data-centre copper demand keeps the price structurally elevated (no material reversion from current levels), TC/RCs stay negative-to-neutral for longer as smelter overcapacity persists, MATSA's sulphide discoveries and Motheo's A1 reserve extend mine life toward management's 15-year target at both operations without a step-change in unit costs, and Kalkaroo's PFS (due within the explicit horizon) confirms a large, low-cost Tier-1-jurisdiction development that the market begins to price as committed growth rather than an option. 46% margin sustained -- close to the FY2025-26 range rather than fully mid-cycle -- because in this scenario the current tailwinds prove more structural than cyclical.

bear.margin_note: A global growth slowdown (China property/construction weakness deepening) pulls copper materially off its current extended level just as TC/RCs snap back positive (new Chinese smelter capacity absorbs the current concentrate shortage, reversing the single largest FY26 tailwind), compressing margins toward or below the FY2023 trough. A second operational incident at either concentrated asset (MATSA underground geotechnical risk, already realised once in Feb-2026, or a Motheo tailings/slope event) or a reserve-life disappointment forces higher sustaining capex per tonne. Kalkaroo's PFS disappoints or the Stage-2 payment is not made, the option lapses, and Black Butte remains stranded, so no growth optionality offsets the margin compression. 30% pre-tax margin -- below any year in the current five-year record except FY2023 -- reflecting both weak commodity prices and a reversal of the TC/RC tailwind simultaneously.

scenario_narratives.base: Sandfire's FY26 result (52.5% EBITDA margin, record US$1.65bn revenue) sits at the confluence of a strong realised copper price and the most favourable treatment/refining-charge environment in years -- FY27's own guidance assumes an even higher forward copper price than FY26 realised, and spot copper is higher again. The base case takes FY27 close to guidance, then fades the margin down through FY2028-31 to a 40% mid-cycle level as copper price and, above all, TC/RCs mean-revert from the current smelter-capacity-glut extreme, while cash tax ramps from FY26's loss-carryforward-depressed 16.6% toward a 28% blended statutory rate as MATSA's post-acquisition tax shelters and Motheo's construction-phase allowances are exhausted. Capex fades from the FY27-guided US$299M peak (which includes discretionary Kalkaroo PFS spend) to a 15% steady state once the MATSA tailings dam and Motheo Stage 4 cutback complete. The axes are the copper price/TC-RC cycle position, whether MATSA and Motheo's targeted 15-year reserve life is achieved through the ongoing sulphide/A1 exploration, and whether Kalkaroo converts from an exclusive option into a funded development.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper's electrification/AI-power demand thesis proves structural rather than cyclical and the price holds near current extended levels rather than reverting; TC/RCs stay favourable for longer as global smelter overcapacity persists; MATSA's sulphide discoveries and Motheo's A1 reserve extend both mines toward the targeted 15-year reserve life without a step-change in unit cost, and Kalkaroo's PFS (due within the horizon) confirms a large, low-cost, Tier-1-jurisdiction development that re-rates the stock from an option to a committed growth project. A 46% margin sustained near the FY2025-26 level, funding continued dividends and Kalkaroo development from the existing net-cash balance sheet without dilution.
scenario_narratives.bear: A global demand slowdown, particularly a deeper Chinese property/construction downturn, pulls copper materially off its current extended price just as new Chinese smelter capacity absorbs the concentrate shortage and reverses the TC/RC tailwind that drove much of FY26's margin expansion -- both of Sandfire's two largest identified financial risks crystallising together. A further operational incident at either concentrated asset (MATSA's underground geotechnical risk, following the Feb-2026 fatality, or a Motheo tailings/slope event) forces higher sustaining capex, while Kalkaroo's PFS disappoints or lapses and Black Butte remains stranded, leaving no growth optionality to offset margin compression. A 30% EBITDA margin -- below any year in the current five-year record bar FY2023 -- with revenue falling as both price and volumes disappoint; the fortress net-cash balance sheet (US$353M) prevents distress but the dividend, only just resumed, would likely be cut or suspended again.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because Sandfire's FY26/FY27 economics rest on two simultaneously favourable, genuinely cyclical conditions -- an elevated copper price sitting above even its own optimistic FY27 guidance, and treatment/refining charges at a multi-year extreme -- either of which reverting materially compresses margins, and both reverting together (the bear case) is a well-precedented commodity-cycle pattern, not a tail risk. Concentration in just two producing assets (MATSA, Motheo) adds idiosyncratic operational risk on top of the commodity cyclicality, and the Feb-2026 fatality is a live reminder that this risk is not merely theoretical. Bull trimmed to 25% because it requires the current price/TC-RC tailwind to prove structural rather than cyclical, which is a minority case for smelter-driven TC/RC cycles historically. Base 45% (below the 50% default) reflecting that the mid-cycle base case is itself already a meaningfully below-consensus, below-FY26 forecast, so the residual probability mass is genuinely split rather than concentrated on the base path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A single-commodity copper miner two years into its current asset base (MATSA acquired May-2022, Motheo first production Feb-2023) is worth its mid-cycle owner cash flow at a mid-cycle price and TC/RC assumption, not its FY2026 record year, which sits at the confluence of an elevated copper price (above even Sandfire's own optimistic FY27 guidance, itself below current spot) and a multi-year-extreme favourable TC/RC environment. The model builds each year from components (revenue x EBITDA margin fading from FY26's 52.5% to a 40% mid-cycle floor - SBC - D&A - a cash tax rate ramping from FY26's loss-shelter-depressed 16.6% to a 28% blended statutory rate + D&A add-back - capex fading from the FY27-guided peak to a 15% steady state - working capital), and caps the terminal value at 12x owner FCF given genuine reserve-life and exploration optionality (Kalkaroo, MATSA sulphides, Motheo A1) beyond a plain single-commodity major. It charges leases once (as debt; immaterial at 1.5% of revenue), SBC once (expensed at a trivial 0.33% of revenue against a flat 465.6m diluted count), and risk once (in the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight, at a single 11.0% USD WACC). All values are computed in USD and converted to AUD at 1.4249 for comparison with the ASX price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper price path: FY26 realised ~US$11,900-12,017/t, FY27 guidance assumes US$13,280/t, and COMEX spot is higher still (~US$14,880/t equivalent) as of the valuation date -- the base case's 40% mid-cycle margin assumption is a judgment that this extended price environment partially reverts; each 10% move in the sustained realised price is roughly 8-9pp of EBITDA margin at Sandfire's cost structure

TC/RC reversal: the single largest identified swing factor -- spot terms near -US$126.80/t (a credit to miners) reflect a global smelter-capacity glut that is itself cyclical; new Chinese smelter capacity absorbing concentrate supply would swing TC/RCs back toward a cost, directly compressing margin

Two-asset concentration: MATSA (Spain, underground, first-ever fatality Feb-2026) and Motheo (Botswana, open-pit) are the only two producing assets; an extended shutdown, grade shortfall or tailings/geotechnical event at either has an outsized group-wide impact with no diversification to fall back on

Cash tax normalisation: FY26's 16.6% cash rate reflects MATSA-acquisition and Motheo-construction tax shelters being drawn down; the model assumes these exhaust by FY2030 and the rate ramps to 28% -- a slower exhaustion would understate near-term FCF versus the model, a faster one would overstate it

Kalkaroo and Black Butte remain optionality, not owned production: Kalkaroo is an exclusive option pending a further Havilah payment and a positive PFS (~US$70M spend committed), and Black Butte has sat undeveloped for years; the 12x terminal cap already gives some credit for this optionality without assuming conversion

FX: AUD/EUR/BWP-denominated costs (Australian corporate overhead, Spanish MATSA opex, Botswana pula Motheo opex) against USD revenue create ongoing translation exposure that can compress margins if the AUD or EUR strengthens against the USD; the AUD quote also moves the AUD-denominated IV one-for-one with the USD/AUD rate even when the USD valuation is unchanged

DeGrussa legacy liability: closure/rehabilitation and unresolved Yugunga-Nya cultural heritage obligations are an open-ended cost from a non-revenue asset, not sized in this model beyond being embedded in the corporate cost line
Dividend resumption (first since 2022, 35 AUD cents FY26 final) signals confidence but is early -- the bear case implies a cut or suspension if the price/TC-RC tailwind reverses as modelled
